observation_summary: The type checker incorrectly allowed access to properties on record types that were not defined on them, because it was conflating properties from unrelated record types during type inference/checking.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves introducing a 'synthetic' flag to distinguish between user-declared record types and those created internally by the compiler for bookkeeping. The logic in JSTypeRegistry was updated to skip these synthetic types when checking for property existence, and the RecordType/RecordTypeBuilder classes were updated to correctly track and propagate this 'declared' vs 'synthetic' state. This is a correction of the underlying type-checking algorithm/methodology used to determine property validity across record types.
evidence_used: The fix modifies JSTypeRegistry to skip synthetic record types when checking for property existence.
The fix adds a 'declared' flag to RecordType and RecordTypeBuilder to distinguish between user-defined and synthetic types.
The fix updates the constructor and property definition logic in RecordType to handle synthetic properties differently.
The fix updates RecordTypeBuilder to allow marking a record type as synthesized.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves the relationship between record types, the root cause is the incorrect algorithmic logic used to determine if a property exists on a type, which failed to account for synthetic types.
The fix adds internal state (the 'declared' flag) to existing classes, but this is a refinement of the existing type-checking algorithm rather than a missing design-level capability.
